passage:
Thursday, 11 pm.
Day twelve. Tenzin and I passed each other in the kitchen tonight like two polite flatmates, not like a husband and his wife. "Salt?" "Here." That was our whole conversation. Neither of us has mentioned the fight about his job offer in Delhi. I keep thinking he should be the one to bring it up, since he went silent first. I bet he's thinking I should, since I stopped talking too. So we wait. The house is so quiet I can hear the clock in the hall. What scares me is what happens if we do talk and it goes like last time: shouting, slammed doors. So I don't. And the gap between us gets a little wider every night.
— Nirmala

qa.q: What was their whole conversation in the kitchen?
What is Nirmala scared of that keeps her from raising the job offer?
qa.a: She fears that talking will go like last time, with shouting and slammed doors, so she stays quiet.

qa.q: What small step could break this freeze?
qa.a: One of them could name the stuck feeling without blame, like "I miss you, and I'm scared of fighting again", and agree on a pause rule.

qa.q: What might Tenzin be thinking during these twelve days?
qa.a: Nirmala guesses he is also waiting for her to move first, since she stopped talking too, so both are held by pride.

grounding: Shows a married couple both avoiding the subject in a quiet house, each waiting for the other, held by pride and fear of another bad fight.

passage:
Pranav: gas cylinder guy coming at 11
Ishita: ok
Pranav: will be late tonight
Ishita: ok
(Two days later)
Ishita: your mom called. call her back
Pranav: ok
Ishita: milk's finished
Pranav: will get
Ishita typed "can we talk about Sunday?" and deleted it. What if he says something worse than last time?
Pranav typed "I miss you" and deleted it. Why should I go first? She walked out, not me.
Ishita: also the plumber needs 500
Pranav: ok. transferring
(Night. Same flat, separate rooms.)
Neither message was ever sent. Both phones lay face down, a wall apart.

qa.q: What did Ishita type and then delete?
qa.a: She typed "can we talk about Sunday?" and deleted it.

qa.q: Why did Pranav delete "I miss you"?
qa.a: Pride stopped him; he felt Ishita should go first because she walked out.

qa.q: What would help this couple step out of the freeze?
qa.a: Sending either deleted message would be enough to start, ideally with an agreement to pause if it heats up rather than repeat Sunday.

qa.q: What would change if Ishita knew Pranav had typed "I miss you"?
qa.a: She would see he misses her too and isn't cold, which could ease her fear of making things worse.

grounding: Shows a couple texting only practical things while each deletes an attempt to reach out, stuck by pride and fear of another fight.
